description: Immigration judges weigh a fixed address in the US, length of residence, family ties, employment history, record of court appearance, criminal record and manner of entry - all to decide danger and flight risk.

The BIA upheld denial of bond where the respondent had no family, employment or community ties and no probable path to lawful status. He had only recently arrived, and the record contained no evidence of family ties, employment history, community ties or court-appearance record in the United States.
energy_note: The fact pattern of every new arrival, treated as a reason to detain.
notes: This is the legal anchor for the 'my parents are in Iran so I cannot get out' problem. Absence of family here is the stated ground.

description: Immigration bond does NOT legally require a US-citizen relative to post it - anyone can pay, including friends or a bond agent. The obstacle is the discretionary flight-risk finding and the amount, not a bar on who may pay.
energy_note: Worth knowing: the rule people believe is not the rule.

aspect: EXAMPLE - no criminal record is not enough
description: Practitioners report flight-risk findings based on adverse credibility, refusal to sign documents, and lack of close relatives in the US who are citizens - with no criminal history at all.
energy_note: Clean record, still detained, for who is not standing behind you.

aspect: EXAMPLE - faulted for not having character references
description: A Kentucky investigation found judges denying bond or setting unpayable amounts, citing short residence. In one case a judge acknowledged no criminal history but faulted the person for not providing letters attesting to character in the community they had only just joined.
energy_note: Asked for character references from a community you arrived in last month.

description: The statutory minimum is USD 1,500, but judges routinely set 5,000, 10,000 or 15,000, and cases exist well over 20,000 - payable in full to ICE by cashier's check, from a person whose money is in a country with no banking link.
energy_note: A sum that must arrive from a country that cannot wire money.

description: The workaround is non-family community ties: leases, sponsor affidavits, employment letters, school records and letters from respected community figures - all of which take time a detained person does not have.
energy_note: Assembling a life's worth of references from a detention phone.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and in one circuit it is worse
description: The Fifth Circuit's interpretation in Buenrostro-Mendez v. Bondi renders traditional equitable considerations - family ties, employment, length of residence - legally irrelevant for those it covers. Which circuit detains you changes what evidence even counts.
energy_note: The geography of your arrest decides which arguments exist.

aspect: SCENARIO - the bond he could not make a case for
description: Omid is detained after a status lapse caused by a filing error. At the bond hearing the judge asks who in the United States can speak to his character and ties. He has been in the country fourteen months. His parents are in Tehran. His only referee is a lab manager who has known him since September. Bond is set at USD 15,000.
energy_note: Detained for the crime of having arrived recently.
